inputs.text: Abinader’s government has signed an agreement in Paris with OECD chief Mathias Cormann to design the Dominican Republic’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy. That matters because corruption shifts public resources away from services people depend on, with the greatest harm falling on those who already have the least power. But an international framework is no substitute for confronting the institutions and entrenched interests that allow corruption to persist. The test is whether ordinary people gain real power to hold officials accountable—not whether the government can announce a strategy.
